transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. 

Between my work and other projects, there's just a lot to juggle—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, various team decisions—and I can't seem to prioritize any of it. I always end up just starting on whatever is the loudest at that exact moment, instead of focusing on what actually matters. It's getting really frustrating.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things that usually matter to you?

No, not really. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself because of how disorganized I am, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed. And I haven't lost interest in my projects at all. I still really want to do them, which is probably why it's so annoying that I can't just sit down and focus on the right things. So, no, it's not a lack of interest, just... a lack of execution, I guess.

Can you tell me more about how you manage tasks that require sustained attention or organization? For example, do you often lose track of time, forget important details, or feel overwhelmed even when starting something simple?

I definitely struggle with the details. Like at work—I'm a software developer—and when I have to do code reviews, which takes a lot of sustained focus, I'll often miss something embarrassingly small. 

I'll completely overlook a reversed condition, or maybe a wrong version number in a dependency file. And then later, when it gets caught, I look back and I can see it was right there in front of me the whole time. I just... I just completely skimmed past it. It's like my brain just won't lock onto those small pieces of information, even when I know I need to be paying close attention.

Do you experience similar difficulties with organization and attention in other areas of your life, like managing personal tasks, household responsibilities, or even following through with plans with friends or family?

Not really, no. I haven't noticed it being much of an issue outside of work and my projects. 

With household responsibilities or, you know, making plans with family and friends... I don't know, I seem to manage that fine. Or at least, no one has complained to me about it. It really just seems to be when I have to sit down and organize all those moving parts for my career or the gallery prep that I hit a wall. So, no, I wouldn't say I have those same difficulties in my personal life.
When you think back to your childhood, did you have similar difficulties with focus or organization, or was this something that started more recently in adulthood?

Looking back... yeah, this was definitely there in grade school, too. It's not just a recent thing. I remember my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I had this bad habit of actually finishing my assignments and then just... forgetting to turn them in. Or I'd completely lose my homework folders. So, yeah, this was happening long before I was even a teenager.

This pattern is most consistent with F90.0 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type).
